This integral doesn't look like one of the basic ones. However, we can manipulate the numerator a bit  to make it look more like the denominator, which reveals a more familiar expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1} & =\frac{3{x}^{2}+3-3}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{3({x}^{2}+1)-3}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{3({x}^{2}+1)}{{x}^{2}+1}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{3\cancel{({x}^{2}+1)}}{\cancel{{x}^{2}+1}}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =3-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Remembering that

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x,
$$

we can now calculate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+1})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x-3\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
